body:
The parent issue with description is #2690 

Proposed level changes for requirement in chapter "V14 Configuration"

Full list of requirements for the chapter is listed here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x22-V14-Config.md

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **14.1.3** | [MODIFIED] Verify that configuration hardening is performed on all third-party products, libraries, frameworks and services as per their individual recommendations. | 2 > 3 |
| **14.1.6** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 14.2.2, SPLIT FROM 4.3.2] Verify that all unneeded features, documentation, sample applications, configurations, and file or directory metadata (such as Thumbs.db, .DS_Store) are removed. | 1 > 3 |
| **14.1.7** | [ADDED] Verify that production environment does not include test code. | 2 > 3 |
| **14.3.2** | [MODIFIED] Verify that debug modes are disabled in production environments for every component to prevent exposure of debug features and unintended information leakage. | 1 > 2 |
| **14.3.3** | [MODIFIED] Verify that the application does not expose detailed version information of server-side components. | 1 > 3 |
| **14.3.4** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 4.3.2] Verify that directory browsing is disabled unless deliberately desired. | 1 > 2 |
| **14.3.5** | [GRAMMAR, MOVED FROM 12.5.1] Verify that the web tier is configured to serve only files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information and source code leakage. For example, backup files (.bak), temporary working files (.swp), compressed files (.zip, .tar.gz) and other extensions commonly used by editors should be blocked unless required. | 1 > 3 |
| **14.3.6** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 14.5.1] Verify that the HTTP TRACE method is disabled to avoid potential information leakage. | 1 > 2 |
| **14.7.4** | [GRAMMAR, MOVED FROM 12.6.1] Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allowlist of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data or files from. | 1 > 2 |
| **14.8.2** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 6.4.2] Verify that key material is not exposed to the application (neither the front-end nor the back-end) but instead uses an isolated security module like a vault for cryptographic operations. | 2 > 3 |
| **14.8.3** | [ADDED] Verify that key secrets have defined expiration dates and are rotated on a schedule based on the organization’s threat model and business requirements. | 2 > 3 |

comments.body:
14.1.3 is a very high risk problem if you get it wrong. It can lead to a lot of problems. Perhaps keep it at L2?

| # | Description | Level change |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **14.1.3** | [MODIFIED] Verify that configuration hardening is performed on all third-party products, libraries, frameworks and services as per their individual recommendations. | 2 > 3 |

I don't have too strong an opinion is it L2 or L3, it really depends on which component we take it as an example and what level of details we are talking about.

What leads to L3, is the potential amount of work to be done (for implementation AND verification). Also, from this point of view, if you have "usual security hardening" in place from other requirements in ASVS, then we can watch this requirement as an extra step further and fine-tune security per used component.
I like your argument for making it L3, Elar.
